summary: KITE abstracts 1,325 reviewed bug mechanisms from historical Java real-bug records (Bears, Bugs.jar, GitBug-Java, GHRB, non-benchmark Defects4J projects), recalls mechanisms that structurally/semantically fit a focal method, injects them as compilable synthetic bugs, and uses those injected methods as kill targets to iteratively strengthen LLM-generated unit tests. On 172 single-method Defects4J bugs with GPT-5.4 it reports a 72.67% real-bug detection rate versus 52.33% for the best baseline (MutGen).

claims.claim: KITE reaches 72.67% real-bug detection rate (RBDR), +20.34 pp over MutGen and +24.41 pp over CoverUp
claims.evidence: Table II: RBDR KITE 72.67, MutGen 52.33, CoverUp 48.26, KTester 47.09, ChatUniTest 45.35, Direct 23.26, EvoSuite 29.07; Table III gains on all five projects (+12.96 to +28.12 pp). Single run, one model, no CIs; with n=172 one task is ~0.58 pp.

claims.claim: Coverage and mutation score do not predict real-bug detection
claims.evidence: Table II: KTester has highest MS (56.72) and BC (74.24) but RBDR 47.09; KITE MS 52.90 with RBDR 72.67.

claims.claim: Synthetic-bug feedback is the main contributor
claims.evidence: Table IV: removing SBF drops RBDR 72.67 -> 52.91 (-19.76 pp); context retrieval -2.32, structural or semantic recall -4.07 each.

claims.claim: KITE finds 19 bugs no other method detects
claims.evidence: Fig. 6 overlap: KITE 125 detections, 19 unique; next best unique count 3.
Table II: 0.177M tokens per focal method vs 0.105-0.107M for MutGen/CoverUp; no dollar or wall-clock numbers; baselines not budget-matched.

patterns.note: Execution against injected synthetic bugs is a stronger feedback signal than coverage or generic mutants for real-bug detection.
Iterative test enhancement driven by executable kill targets; tests are generated against the correct version only.
Semantic recall of bug mechanisms from a knowledge base; ablation -4.07 pp.
Structural recall over AST-derived structure index records; ablation -4.07 pp.

methodology.sample: 172 single-method real bugs from five Defects4J projects (Cli, Compress, Csv, JacksonDatabind, Jsoup), filtered from 305
methodology.baselines: Direct LLM, ChatUniTest, CoverUp, MutGen, KTester, EvoSuite; some reimplemented by the authors from paper descriptions ('otherwise reproduce the core workflow')
methodology.contamination_controls: Knowledge base excludes benchmark projects (project-level leakage control); no control for GPT-5.4 memorization of well-known Defects4J bugs

standards.artifacts: No code or data link found in the text

biases.detail: Defects4J bugs and fixes are public and likely in GPT-5.4 training data; mechanism-recall prompting may surface memorized fixes more than baselines do.
Some baselines reimplemented by the authors; not budget-matched (KITE uses ~70% more tokens than MutGen).
Restricted to bugs localized to a single method; multi-method and cross-file bugs excluded (§V).

coi.detail: Academic authors evaluating their own method.

verdict_reason: Clear Java evaluation with a meaningful primary metric (real-bug detection rather than coverage), useful ablation and overlap analysis; weakened by single model/single run, Defects4J memorization risk, partly reimplemented and non-budget-matched baselines, and no artifacts.
applicability: Relevant to the Java team's test-generation loop: it argues against gating agent-written tests on line coverage or generic mutation score alone, and for seeding tests with the team's own historical defect classes (e.g. schema edge cases, encoding/escaping, null/empty sections in domain examples) turned into executable 'should-fail' variants. A cheap version is a curated bug-mechanism catalogue per repositoriesitory plus PIT custom mutators. It is single-method and single-repo, so it says nothing about cross-repo contract bugs between the services and downstream, and it costs roughly 0.18M tokens per method, which matters at the scale of several repositories.

conflicts_with.detail: TestAgent uses mutation score as its main fault-detection evidence (83.69%); KITE shows mutation score does not track real-bug detection (KTester highest MS but 25.58 pp lower RBDR).
